headline: AWS unveils new tools for managing AI agents with AgentCore and Bedrock enhancements.

items.title: Understanding Amazon Bedrock model lifecycle
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock introduces a feature for managing foundational model (FM) transitions, ensuring AI applications remain operational during model evolutions. This includes understanding the three lifecycle states and leveraging the extended access feature for smooth migrations. Practical strategies for transitioning applications are discussed, offering a robust framework for developers to maintain AI continuity in dynamic environments.
items.why_it_matters: Ensures AI systems remain stable and effective amidst continuous model updates.

items.title: AWS Agent Registry now in preview
items.summary: AWS has launched a preview of the AWS Agent Registry within AgentCore, designed as a centralized platform for discovering, sharing, and reusing AI agents and their skills across enterprises. This tool aims to streamline the management of AI resources, enhancing collaboration and efficiency in developing complex AI systems.

items.title: GitHub Copilot CLI for Beginners
items.summary: GitHub introduces a beginner-friendly CLI for its Copilot, providing a step-by-step guide for developers to integrate Copilot into their workflows. This release aims to simplify the adoption of AI-assisted coding practices, making it accessible to a broader range of developers.
items.source: The latest on AI & ML - The GitHub Blog

items.title: Embed a live AI browser agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides a new feature to embed live AI-powered browser agents into React applications. This involves generating a Live View URL, rendering streams within the app, and integrating AI agents to automate browsing tasks. Developers can leverage this to enhance user interaction and automate workflows within their applications.

all_items.title: Understanding Amazon Bedrock model lifecycle
all_items.summary: This post shows you how to manage FM transitions in Amazon Bedrock, so you can make sure your AI applications remain operational as models evolve. We discuss the three lifecycle states, how to plan migrations with the new extended access feature, and practical strategies to transition your applications to newer models without disruption.

all_items.title: Embed a live AI browser agent in your React app with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
all_items.summary: This post walks you through three steps: starting a session and generating the Live View URL, rendering the stream in your React application, and wiring up an AI agent that drives the browser while your users watch. At the end, you will have a working sample application you can clone and run.

all_items.title: Introducing stateful MCP client capabilities on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime
all_items.summary: In this post, you will learn how to build stateful MCP servers that request user input during execution, invoke LLM sampling for dynamic content generation, and stream progress updates for long-running tasks. You will see code examples for each capability and deploy a working stateful MCP server to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime.
